title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical error is visible. The 2-cartesian claim is consistent with the local model (Δ*)^E-bundle restricted to a covering branch, since Γ^!_{G,G'} ⊂ Γ^!_{G,G''}.
The page is a sketch: the definition (105) of the iterated 2-fibre product and the identification of the triple object are only asserted, not proved here.
The large diagonal strokes across the page suggest Grothendieck crossed out (superseded) this passage.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum M_G as an extension of the stratum's (twisted) groupoid by Z^{edges} (Dehn twists)
ideas.modern_name: π1 of the deleted neighbourhood of a boundary stratum / 'inertia at infinity'; S_AΠM_G
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore from Bers, Abikoff, Harvey; in the profinite/arithmetic setting Ihara, Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Boggi (1990s–2000s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'structure à l'infini' and tubular neighbourhoods of the boundary; no explicit formulas there

ideas.what: Compatibility of these extensions along chains of générisations G→G'→G'': the triple punctured link is the 2-fibre-product pull-back of ΠM*_{G,G''} along ΠM_{G,G'}→ΠM_{G,G''}
ideas.modern_name: Gluing/descent data of a stratified homotopy type; exit-path 2-category of a stratified stack
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths), Treumann (exit-path 2-categories for stacks, 2009), Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A); for M̄_{g,n} specifically, Boggi and Ebert–Giansiracusa

ideas.what: Twisting of the Z^{A(G)} kernel by the action of Aut G on edges, and quotients Z^C for Γ'-stable edge subsets (continued on next page)
ideas.modern_name: Twisted local system of Dehn twists on the orbifold stratum

missed.claim: Grothendieck organises the homotopy type of M̄_{g,ν} near infinity as a system of groupoids indexed by chains of graph générisations, with 2-cartesian compatibilities. Effectively this is an exit-path 2-category / stratified homotopy description of the DM boundary, predating MacPherson–Treumann–Lurie. The note is explicit about 2-fibre products of groupoids attached to triples G→G'→G''.
missed.quote: le carré cartésien est 2-cartésien. En d'autres termes, le produit 2-cartésien ΠM*_{G,G',G''} défini formellement via (105) ... s'interprète concrètement comme l'extension image inverse de ΠM*_{G,G''} sur ΠM_{G,G''} par ΠM_{G,G'} → ΠM_{G,G''}.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precedent for the stratified/exit-path approach to moduli of curves. It also suggests a combinatorial presentation of the profinite Teichmüller tower (relevant to Grothendieck–Teichmüller actions on boundary data), formulated via 2-limits over the graph poset.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual facts (Dehn-twist extensions, pull-back along branches) are standard. What is mildly notable is the systematic 2-categorical gluing of groupoids over chains of stable graphs, which anticipates exit-path formalisms. The broad idea of a 'structure à l'infini' is however known from the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Diagram (112): the lower-left vertex written 'ΠM_{G#}' is ΠM_{G,G'} (with overstrikes), and the map labelled 'can' goes ΠM_{G,G'} → ΠM_{G,G''}.
'l'extension du groupe [?] inverse' should read 'l'extension image inverse'.
'des deux catégories successives de ΠM_{G,G'}' probably reads 'des deux générisations successives (de ΠM_{G,G'} ...)'.
'une unique [?] généralisation' should read 'une générisation G→G''', and 'spéciale' crossed out is replaced by 'générisation' ('les générisations "les plus grossières"').
'MD discret' refers to the Mumford–Deligne graph with all edges contracted (the coarsest générisation).
The last line is 'On posera S_AΠM_G' (the S_A notation is continued on the next page).
